speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing wrist pain and difficulty moving your hand; please describe exactly where the pain is located and what activities make it worse. To better assess the situation, could you tell me if you have noticed any swelling, redness, or a specific injury that led to these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing pain in her right thumb and wrist, which radiates to her elbow for the past three months. The pain worsens when she holds her infant son and is alleviated somewhat with an ice pack. She mentions a history of falling on her right outstretched hand about six months ago. She also notes that her mother has a history of chronic joint pain treated with methotrexate. The patient has been taking ibuprofen as needed for her symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: De Quervain's tenosynovitis (likely with secondary lateral epicondylitis/tennis elbow given the radiation to the elbow).

The pain in your thumb and wrist that worsens when holding your baby is classic for inflammation of the tendons on the outside of your wrist. The radiation to your elbow suggests the strain may have spread or involved the extensor muscles as well. Since this has persisted for three months despite ibuprofen and ice, do you have any numbness or tingling in your thumb, index, or middle fingers?
